text:
Evidence supports perturbation diagnostics, but does not establish sensitivity as a reliable surrogate for held-out improvement. [Betello et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.13165) report position-dependent damage from history deletions, including substantial NDCG losses; [CASPER](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.12686) shows single training-interaction edits can change many users’ rankings. These involve training-data perturbations, so transfer to frozen-model history probes requires validation. [Cascade-guided adversarial training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.05492) improves both ranking accuracy and robustness on four datasets, demonstrating that joint gains are possible—not that minimizing arbitrary sensitivity guarantees accuracy.

Suggested validation protocol: inject controlled faults such as disabled positional information or corrupted attention masks; verify probes detect them and repairs recover validation HR@10. Include identity edits, deterministic evaluation, and matched edit budgets; repeat deletion, replacement and shuffle draws. Separate legitimate dependence on recent items from harmful instability. Test whether diagnostic changes predict paired HR@10 gains across interventions. Following [paired retrieval evaluation research](https://ciir-publications.cs.umass.edu/getpdf.php?id=744), estimate uncertainty from paired user differences: bootstrap users within each category, recompute the equal-weight four-category macro, and report category effects. Repeated edits of one user are dependent replicates, not additional users. Twenty simulator users provide exploratory evidence only.

Keep the pinned 99-negative evaluation for selection. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog model comparisons, even in expectation; full-catalog recommendation stability therefore measures a different outcome. With 200 users/category, one changed hit moves macro HR@10 by 0.00125. [Adaptive-holdout research](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02629) warns that repeated feedback-driven selection overfits validation. Log every inspected trial, limit hypotheses, and treat ordinary paired intervals as exploratory after selection; reserve confirmatory claims for the host’s untouched final evaluation.
